drawing_plan.help: Upload a drawing at the top and place lighting towers, battens, circles, shapes and text on it. Use the toolbar at the top to pick a drawing tool, and the panel at the bottom to edit the selected element's details. Use the ruler tool to calibrate a known distance so bars are shown at their real length. The dashed frame marks the printable area in the PDF (A4 landscape). You can also freely arrange elements without a drawing.

lighting_tower.empty.desc: Add lighting towers here. You can assign slots to each rack and fill them with circles—that way, you can see at a glance which device needs to be installed where.
lighting_tower.help: This is where you manage your lighting towers (e.g. lighting towers or trusses left/right of stage). Use "New lighting tower" to create one, give it a name, optionally a side (L/R) and its slot count – a slot is one rack position. Then click a slot to assign it a circuit number, so you can see at a glance which device needs to be mounted where. Use the pencil icon to edit a rack later, the bookmark icon to save it as a template, and "Insert from template" to quickly re-create a saved rack. Elements are included in the PDF export.

batten.empty.desc: Add the components of your overhead machinery here and place circles at specific locations on them—that way, you can see at a glance which device needs to be installed where.
batten.help: This is where you manage your overhead rigging: bars, trusses and point hoists. Use "Add element" to create a new one, giving it a name, length and optionally height. Use the circle button to place fixtures at specific positions on the bar or truss (position 0 = center) and link them to a circuit number. Use the bookmark icon to save an element as a template, and "Insert from template" to add a saved one back in. Elements are included in the PDF export.
